rationale: Lens: contract stability. The three named facts of the R5.1 basis are individually TRUE, verified live at 694b9d46: (a) .mindspec/session.json is gitignored (.gitignore:3, confirmed via git check-ignore); (b) .beads/issues.jsonl is the sole artifactPaths entry (internal/next/guard.go:24-26) and is exempted before the entanglement split (CheckDirtyTreeProportional delegates to CheckDirtyTreeDetail, which normalizes artifact dirt via bd export exactly as before); (c) the bead worktree dir is created at Step 5.5, after the Step 1 guard, and .worktrees/ is gitignored (.gitignore:67). CheckDirtyTree/CheckDirtyTreeDetail are untouched, so release.go and spec approve keep all-blocks semantics. AC-16's backfillExistingEpicPhase is sound against bead-1/bead-2: WithPhaseWriteLock is non-reentrant but ApproveSpec holds no outer lock and never calls EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 (only complete.go:554, plan.go:335, impl.go:296 do), so no self-block; the stored=="" check matches phaseReadOutcome's documented contract (absent OR present-but-invalid both surface as Stored:""); a concurrent claim's phase advance serializes on the same lock and either lands first (later phase left untouched) or second (forward overwrite of plan) — no stale-over-fresh window. The five AC-16 legs are honest and genuinely red-on-revert (the later-phase legs assert ZERO MergeMetadata calls, which the pre-128 unconditional write fails). Spec approve's existing-epic idempotence (warn + skip creation) is preserved verbatim. HOWEVER, the derivation's COMPLETENESS claim — 'exactly (a)(b)(c), so the set is EMPTY today' — is falsified by live code on the very claim path it traces: Step 7.5 (cmd/mindspec/next.go:373-377) writes TRACKED, non-gitignored paths in the invoking checkout when recording is enabled (finding F1). That is the load-bearing claim of the removed block, so this is REQUEST_CHANGES, not a nit. Not a hard block: blast radius is conditional (recording.enabled defaults false, off in this repo, feature dormant since spec 071) and the fix is a normal round's work.
concrete_changes_required: F1: Correct the R5.1 enumeration for the recording marker writes. Step 7.5 of the claim path (cmd/mindspec/next.go:373-377) calls recording.EmitBeadMarker + recording.AddBeadToPhase, which write .mindspec/specs/<spec>/recording/events.ndjson (append) and manifest.json (read-modify-write via ReadManifest/WriteManifest) in the INVOKING checkout whenever config recording.enabled is true and the spec has a recording dir — which spec create builds automatically when enabled (internal/spec/create.go:160). These paths are TRACKED, not gitignored (git check-ignore exits 1; specs 036-071 have committed recording/ files). So in a recording-enabled install, dirty manifest.json/events.ndjson is genuinely claim-entangleable user dirt — the read-modify-write of manifest.json absorbs and rewrites the user's uncommitted state — yet the shipped code classifies it ignoredDirt and proceeds. Acceptable dispositions: (i) make the enumeration per-spec-aware and include the two recording paths for the target spec; (ii) a rationale-carrying exemption declaring recording files machine-managed telemetry — but that must amend the spec/ADR text, since ADR-0025's artifact model is 'named, not a glob' and does not currently cover them; or (iii) at absolute minimum, correct the guard.go comment and the spec-side derivation to state the conditional fourth write class and its accepted residual. Whatever the choice, the current 'exactly (a)(b)(c)' text is unsound as written.

F1b: Add a recording-enabled leg to the AC-8(ii) enumeration pin (enable recording in the fixture config + create the spec so StartRecording builds the recording dir, then claim). The pin's honesty is fixture-conditional: it derives what a real claim writes under the FIXTURE's config, and with recording off it structurally cannot observe conditional writes — the exact class F1 exhibits. Without this leg the anti-drift test stays green while the enumeration is wrong today.

findings.title: R5.1 derived enumeration misses the claim path's recording writes to tracked paths
findings.detail: The guard.go comment and spec R5.1 claim the worktree-creating claim writes exactly session.json (gitignored), issues.jsonl (exempt artifact), and the worktree dir (post-guard, gitignored). Verified live: all three facts hold, but the enumeration is incomplete. next.go Step 7.5 writes .mindspec/specs/<spec>/recording/{events.ndjson,manifest.json} — tracked, non-ignored, in the invoking checkout — gated only on recording.enabled config plus a recording dir that spec create builds automatically when enabled. The feature is live (StartRecording at internal/spec/create.go:160; markers also emitted by complete and both approves) and historical recording files are committed through spec 071. A user with recording enabled and uncommitted recording-file dirt gets that dirt entangled by the claim's read-modify-write after the guard waved it through as ignoredDirt — the precise failure class the removed block existed to prevent, and one the pre-bead all-dirt block DID catch. The AC-8(ii) pin cannot go red on this because its fixture runs with recording disabled.

findings.title: AC-8(iii) seam leg never exercises next.go's refusal wiring
findings.detail: SetEntangleableClaimPathsForTest is used only inside internal/next/entangle_test.go, which drives CheckDirtyTreeProportional and DirtyTreeFailure directly. Nothing tests cmd/mindspec/next.go's blockingDirt branch (next.go:138-144); the e2e tests run the binary as a subprocess where the seam is unreachable, and with the real enumeration empty that branch is dead in every delivered test. A mutant deleting the refusal branch (or routing blockingDirt into the notice) passes the full suite. The classification and the DirtyTreeFailure message contract ARE pinned, so this is the 3-line wiring only — but this repo's red-on-revert discipline is the point of AC-8(iii), and 'the claim refuses' (spec text) is not what the delivered test drives. Suggest an in-process command-execution leg using the seam, or a recorded rationale accepting the residual.

findings.title: Backfill message says 'stored phase was empty' for the present-but-invalid case too
findings.detail: backfillExistingEpicPhase's stored=="" branch covers both a genuinely absent mindspec_phase and a present-but-invalid value (phaseReadOutcome's contract, correctly relied on and documented). But the emitted message 'phase backfilled: plan (stored phase was empty)' is literally false in the invalid-value case — the field was present, just unusable. R3.6's theme is output honesty; 'was empty or invalid' would be exact. The wireBackfillFixture doc comment itself notes no test leg exercises the present-but-invalid combination.

findings.title: AC-16 interaction surface verified clean
findings.detail: No deadlock: WithPhaseWriteLock is non-reentrant but ApproveSpec's existing-epic path acquires it exactly once and calls no other lock-taking function (EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 is never called from spec approve; EnsureMigrated is invoked ahead of impl/plan/complete preflights only). No double-write: the backfill writes at most once, conditional on the fresh under-lock stored value, and the three no-op legs assert zero MergeMetadata calls. Concurrent claim-advance serializes on the same repo-scoped lock with only benign ordering residual. Spec approve idempotence (existing epic warns and skips creation) preserved. Bead worktree left byte-identical (git status clean, 0 entries).
